v2 - u2 = 2aS₂

questions.question: What type of maintenance is most effective?
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

Maintenance of machinery means its upkeep and repair in the event of a breakdown.

It also includes the renewal and replacement of damaged parts.

 
 

 
 
**Breakdown maintenance**

 
 
 
 
• It is a type of maintenance used for equipment **after equipment break** down or malfunction is often the most expensive
 
 
 
 

 
 
**Preventive maintenance**

 
 
 
 
• It is regularly performed on a piece of equipment to **lessen the likelihood of it failing**.
 
• It is performed while the equipment is still working so that it does not break down unexpectedly.
 
• It is a most effective maintenance
 
 
 
 

 
 
**Predictive maintenance**

 
 
 
 
• It is first to predict when equipment failure might occur, and secondly, to **prevent the occurrence of the failure** by performing maintenance.
 
• Monitoring for future failure allows maintenance to be planned before the failure occurs.
 
 
 
 

 
 
**Shutdown Maintenance**

 
 
 
 
• **Shutdown Maintenance** is **maintenance** that can only be performed while equipment is not in use. 
 
• **Shutting down** machinery can be costly, but sometimes due to the nature of the defective part/machine, **shutdown maintenance** is the only viable **maintenance** procedure.
 
 
 
 

 
 
**Corrective Maintenance**

 
 
 
 
• This type of maintenance is carried out to correct errors that were not discovered during the product development phase.
 
 
 
 

 
 
**Perfective Maintenance**

 
 
 
 
• This type of maintenance is carried out to enhance the functionalities of the system based on the customer’s request.
 
 
 
 

 
 
**Adaptive Maintenance**

 
 
 
 
• Adaptive maintenance is usually required for porting the software to work in a new environment such as work on a new computer platform or with a new operating system
 
 
 
 

**Preventive maintenance consists of:**

 
• Proper plans and installation of machine/equipment
 
• Periodic inspection of the plant, equipment, and machines
 
• Repetitive servicing, upkeep, and overhauling
 
• Adequate lubrication, cleaning, and painting

questions.question: _______ is a process of case hardening in which the outer layer is made hard by increasing amount of carbon.
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

Case hardening is a method used to harden the outer surface of low-carbon steel while leaving the center or core soft and ductile. Case hardening involves heating the metal to its critical temperature in some carbonaceous material. The following methods are commonly used:

 
• **Carburizing**
 
• Cyaniding
 
• Nitriding
 
• Induction Hardening
 
• Flame hardening

**Carburizing**

__
 
• Carburizing is one of the most widely used surface-hardening processes.
 
• The process involves diffusing carbon into low-carbon steel to form a high-carbon steel surface.
 
• The Carburizing process is also referred to as case hardening or case carburizing process.
 
• It is a heat treatment process that produces a surface that is resistant to wear while maintaining the toughness and strength of the core.
 
• High Carbon Steels have higher strength and hardness.
 
• Low-carbon steels have higher toughness.
 
• **Increasing carbon only on the surface of low-carbon steel can give a hard surface and tough core.****​**__

**Tempering **

 
• Tempering is the process of annealing martensite at low temperatures.
 
• Tempering is a heat-treatment process consisting of reheating the hardened steel to a temperature below 400°C, followed by cooling.
 
• Steel in its hardened condition is generally too brittle to be used for certain functions. Therefore, it is tempered. The aims of tempering are:
 
 
• to relieve the internal stresses
 
• to regulate the hardness and toughness
 
• to decrease the brittleness
 
• to restore some ductility
 
• to induce shock resistance
 
 

**Annealing**

 
• Annealing is a heat treatment process in which the material is taken to a high temp, kept there for some time, and then **cooled in the furnace itself.**
 
• Cooling is done slowly to avoid distortion.
 
• The benefits of annealing are:
 
 
• Relieve stresses
 
• Increase softness, ductility, and toughness
 
• Produce a specific microstructure
 
• Improve machining characteristic
 
 

Normalizing

 
• Heat the steel from 30°C to 50°C above its upper critical temp, held for about fifteen minutes, and then allowed it to cool down in still air. 
 
• The homogeneous structure provides a higher yield point, ultimate tensile strength, and impact strength with lower ductility to steel.
 
• The main purpose of normalizing is 
 
 
• Refine grain size in metal, improve strength and hardness, reduce ductility
 
• Remove cold work stress.
 
• Remove dislocations due to hot working.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a non-return valve in a water pipe line?
questions.solution:

Valves: 

 
• A valve is a device, which controls and regulates the start, finish, direction, and pressure of the flow of air.
 
• There are five types of valves used in pneumatics and hydraulics
 
• Valves are divided into 5 groups according to their function:

 
 

 
 
Directional Valves (Way Valves)

 
 
 
It influences the path, taken by the air stream. It controls the start, stop and direction of the flow of air.

 
 
 

 
 
Non – Return Valve

 
 
 
It stops the flow in one direction and permit flow in the opposite direction.

 
 
 

 
 
Pressure control Valve

 
 
 
It is used in hydraulic systems to control actuator force (force = pressure × area)

 
and to determine and select pressure levels at which certain machine operations must occur

 
 
 

 
 
Flow control Valve

 
 
 
It is used to regulate the flow rate and pressure of liquids or gases through a pipeline.

 
 
 

 
 
Shut-off Valve

 
 
 
It is designed for and capable of positive closure to prevent flow within a piping system.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a globe valve in a pipeline?

options.text: It provide strength to the joint
It avoids water from getting heated

questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

There are the following types of valves:

**Gate Valve**

 
• A Gate valve is a linear motion valve that uses a typically flat closure element perpendicular to the process flow, which slides into the flow stream to provide shut-off.
 
• With a Gate valve, the direction of fluid flow does not change, and the diameter through which the process fluid passes is essentially equal to that of the pipe.
 
• Hence, Gate valves tend to have minimal pressure drop when opened fully.
 
• In general, Gate valves are not used to regulate fluid flow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/11079aca009842d8f3ce54439b476428ec5cb7f4a782af9a75cec5b3cf106dce.png] 

**Globe valve**

 
• A Globe valve is a linear motion valve characterized by a body with a longer face-to-face that accommodates flow passages sufficiently long enough to ensure a smooth flow through the valve without any sharp turns.
 
• Globe valves are widely used to regulate fluid flow in both ON/OFF and throttling services.
 
• The direction of fluid flow through the valve changes several times, which increases the pressure drop across the valve.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c0132629b72c1b269971eec3d0277c8af225c4059b2e9e190e96dc1973af3bac.png] 

**Plug Valve**

 
• They are similar to Gates and work particularly well in abrasive services.
 
• These are available either lubricated or non-lubricated.

**Ball Valve**

 
• Ball valves are quarter-turn, straight-through flow valves, and limited to moderate temperature service (below 250°C) by the plastic seats that create a seal around the ball.
 
• The type of seat can vary with the valve pressure rating and materials of construction.
 
• They have found applications in flow control, as well as ON/OFF use in isolating a pipe stream.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/859c82b7f527e42d5b09a9844e093f019c9adf085909980049976f7f5cbfc3ca.png] 

**Check valve**

 
• These valves are used to check the flow of water in the reverse direction.
 
• These are generally provided on the delivery side of the pump.
 
• These valves work automatically.

**Relief Valve**

 
• It is a type of safety valve used to control or limit the pressure in a system, pressure might otherwise build up and create a process upset, instrument or equipment failure, or fire.
 
• The pressure is relieved by allowing the pressurized fluid to flow from an auxiliary passage out of the system.

questions.question: The difference between the maximum limit of size and minimum limit of size in assembling a product is known as:
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

Nominal size is the size of a part specified in the drawing as a matter of convenience.

Actual size is the actually measured dimension of the part.

Tolerance is the difference between the** upper limit **and the **lower limit** of a dimension.

In other words, it is the maximum permissible variation in a dimension.

The tolerance may be unilateral or bilateral.

When all the tolerance is allowed on one side of the nominal size, e.g. 10 ₋ ₀.₀₀₄ ⁺ ⁰.⁰⁰⁰ , then it is said to be a unilateral system of tolerance.

When tolerance is allowed on **both sides** of the nominal size e.g. 10 ₋ ₀.₀₀₄ ⁺ ⁰.⁰⁰⁴, then it is said to be a bilateral system of tolerance.
